problem:
The displacement $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the **magnitude** of the resultant force, in newtons, acting on the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$ Round your final answer **to the nearest integer**.

The magnitude of the resultant force is
{{field-1}} $N.$
worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate $r$ to get the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\frac{1}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(\frac{1}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =2\cdot ⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=2\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(2) & =⟨-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 2),\,-\frac{2}{(2)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4),\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of $F(2)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|F(2)| & =\sqrt{(-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4))^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & ≈6\,\text{N},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

So, the magnitude of the resultant force is $6\,\text{N}.$
